title: Support of an integral element lies in the saturation
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $P$ be a finitely generated submonoid of a torsion-free abelian group $G$, and let $x=\sum_{g\in S}c_ge^g\in k[G]$ with finite support $S$. If $x$ is integral over $k[P]$, then every $g\in S$ lies in $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{h\in G:\exists n>0,\ nh\in P\}$. We use the monoid and group-completion conventions of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and the monomial-basis normalization argument, printed p.104

proof.text:
Fix $g\in S$ and suppose for contradiction that $g
otin P^{\mathrm{sat}}$. Let $T$ be the union of $S$ and the finite supports of all coefficients occurring in one monic equation for $x$ over $k[P]$. Let $H\subseteq G$ be the subgroup generated by the finite set of generators of $P$ together with $T$. It is a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group, so [lem-trf-fg-torsionfree-group-free] gives a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis of $H$. In $V=H\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, let $C$ be the cone generated by the images of the generators of $P$. If $g\otimes1$ belonged to $C$, clearing denominators would give $ng\in P$ for some $n>0$, contradicting $g
otin P^{\mathrm{sat}}$. Thus $g\otimes1
otin C$. By [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite], write $C$ as the common nonnegative locus of finitely many rational linear forms. At least one form $\lambda$ satisfies $\lambda(g\otimes1)<0$; after multiplying by a positive common denominator on the chosen basis, it restricts to a homomorphism $w:H	o\mathbf Z$ with $w(p)\ge0$ for every $p\in P$ and $w(g)<0$. All terms in the equation lie in $k[H]$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and its monomial-basis normalization argument, printed p.104; finite subgroup and rational-cone separation are expanded here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-integral-support-weighted-initial-degree] to this weight, the element $x$ viewed in $k[H]$, and the finite supports in the chosen monic equation. Its hypotheses hold because all monomials of every coefficient in $k[P]$ have nonnegative weight, while $g\in S$ has negative weight. The node therefore says that $x$ cannot be integral over $k[P]$, contradicting the hypothesis. Hence no such $g$ exists, and every element of $S$ lies in $P^{\mathrm{sat}}$.
